project.name: Signal to Insight
project.purpose: Turn high-signal technology sources into durable explanations, reusable patterns, and practical applications.

insights.title: Why enterprise AI agents fail after the POC
insights.one_liner: A production agent needs an execution substrate for controlled work, not just a model connected to tools.

source.title: Why Your Enterprise Tech Stack Isn't Ready for AI Agents

insights.signal: A successful AI proof of concept can still be architecturally far from a production-ready enterprise system.
insights.derived_insight: The reusable unit is not the agent itself. It is the controlled execution environment around the agent: identity, authority, history, data access, human intervention and replay.

patterns.name: Immutable execution history
patterns.purpose: Reconstruct what happened and why without depending on ad-hoc developer logs.

patterns.name: Separated execution and data planes
patterns.purpose: Keep observability and orchestration possible without granting broad access to sensitive business data.

patterns.name: Human-agent task equivalence
patterns.purpose: Model the task independently from the executor so work can move between AI and humans without creating a parallel exception process.

patterns.name: Replayable evaluation
patterns.purpose: Use reconstructable historical cases to compare models, prompts, policies or tools against the same context.

application.question: Can the system explain months later why a customer was changed, under whose authority, using which context and approval?

limitations: An append-only history still needs identity, policy versions, retention, tamper protection and meaningful event semantics.
Separating data and orchestration reduces exposure but does not automatically eliminate prompt injection or data exfiltration.
Human handoff still requires ownership, locking, idempotency, approval authority, timeout and recovery rules.
